liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Viola Lee Blues** (4 reviews): This early show contains the final Viola Lee Blues, which was then retired; Viola Lee into Cumberland Blues is called on fire, the standout jam of the tape [11][13][18][19]
- **Till The Morning Comes** (2 reviews): Played only five times despite being on American Beauty; here it is weak, with many off-key chords; One of only a few attempts at Till The Morning Comes [16][19]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Uncle John's Band as great [13]
- **Hard To Handle** (1 other source): All of Hard To Handle has been patched in on this version [5]
- **Saint Stephen** (1 review): Reviewer likes the slow start to Saint Stephen [22]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Reviewer especially enjoys The Other One [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-10-31.122042.sbd.deluca.Digitalrbb.miller.flac1648** (recommended): soundboard; 46 songs; 260 min; rated 4.71/5 by 7 [1]. Said about its sound: I Know You Rider is cut at the end, and there is a reel flip in Brokedown Palace [1]
- **gd1970-10-31.early-late.sbd.serafin.33566.flac16**: soundboard; 31 songs; 156 min; rated 4.14/5 by 7 [3]. Said about its sound: Early show flaws: I Know You Rider end cut, dropouts in Brokedown Palace and Goin' Down The Road [3]
- **gd70-10-31.late.sbd.cousinit.16902.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 28 songs; 142 min; rated 4.22/5 by 9 [4]. Said about its sound: Late show recording has good sound quality [21]
- **gd70-10-31.early.sbd.fischer.6517.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 13 songs; 69 min; rated 3/5 by 18 [9]. Said about its sound: Reviewer refers to the circulating tapes as hissy old Grateful Dead tapes [18]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says the shown setlist is the late show's, but this recording is actually the early show [11]
- Recording includes the New Riders late-night set, conveying the feel of the whole night [21]
- Recording includes the New Riders set, heard in context alongside the Dead [22]
- Monitor problems led Weir and Pigpen to get rowdy and curse; blame fell on the college radio's sound man [5]
- Sound man Gordon Healy told Jimmy Warburton the problem came from someone stepping on a wire [5]
- Reviewer says apart from the opening Till The Morning Comes, the rest of the show is smokin' [16]
- Reviewer sees the early show as essentially a warm-up for the evening gig, solid but not a classic [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-10-31.122042.sbd.deluca.Digitalrbb.miller.flac1648**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel (7inch @7.5ips 1/2trk) -> Dat (Denon DTR 2000/48k) [1]. Also: Patch source for this version came from Darryl Hinko [1]
- **gd1970-10-31.early-late.sbd.serafin.33566.flac16**: transferred by Jay Serafin; source: A-SBD [3]
- **gd70-10-31.late.sbd.cousinit.16902.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Cousinit; source: Soundboard - Late Show [4]. Also: Late show, including NRPS set, from cassette recorded directly from master reels, transferred via DAT and WAV to SHN; converted by Cousinit [4]
- **gd70-10-31.early.sbd.fischer.6517.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Mike Fischer; source: Soundboard - Early Show [9]
